title: Infinite Maze
statementMd:
We've got a rectangular $*n* × *m*$-cell maze. Each cell is either passable, or is a wall (impassable). A little boy found the maze and cyclically tiled a plane with it so that the plane became an infinite maze. Now on this plane cell $(*x*, *y*)$ is a wall if and only if cell ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5820f73507b71bbab0564415ed80476b7cbd4b71.png) is a wall.

In this problem ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6dd276f849101e7efda6cb8031d4056744d532a1.png) is a remainder of dividing number $*a*$ by number $*b*$.

The little boy stood at some cell on the plane and he wondered whether he can walk infinitely far away from his starting position. From cell $(*x*, *y*)$ he can go to one of the following cells: $(*x*, *y* - 1)$, $(*x*, *y* + 1)$, $(*x* - 1, *y*)$ and $(*x* + 1, *y*)$, provided that the cell he goes to is not a wall.

## Input

The first line contains two space-separated integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 1500$) — the height and the width of the maze that the boy used to cyclically tile the plane.

Each of the next $*n*$ lines contains $*m*$ characters — the description of the labyrinth. Each character is either a "`#`", that marks a wall, a "`.`", that marks a passable cell, or an "`S`", that marks the little boy's starting point.

The starting point is a passable cell. It is guaranteed that character "`S`" occurs exactly once in the input.

## Output

Print "`Yes`" (without the quotes), if the little boy can walk infinitely far from the starting point. Otherwise, print "`No`" (without the quotes).

## Note

In the first sample the little boy can go up for infinitely long as there is a "clear path" that goes vertically. He just needs to repeat the following steps infinitely: up, up, left, up, up, right, up.

In the second sample the vertical path is blocked. The path to the left doesn't work, too — the next "copy" of the maze traps the boy.
statementZhMd:
我们有一个矩形的 $*n* × *m*$ 个单元格组成的迷宫。每个单元格要么可以通行，要么是墙（不可通行）。一个小男孩发现了这个迷宫，并用它周期性地铺满整个平面，于是平面变成了一个无限迷宫。现在，在这个平面上，当且仅当单元格 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5820f73507b71bbab0564415ed80476b7cbd4b71.png) 是墙时，单元格 $(*x*, *y*)$ 才是墙。

在本题中，![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6dd276f849101e7efda6cb8031d4056744d532a1.png) 表示数字 $*a*$ 除以数字 $*b*$ 所得的余数。

小男孩站在平面上的某个单元格中，他想知道自己是否能够无限地走到远离起点的位置。从单元格 $(*x*, *y*)$ 出发，他可以前往以下单元格之一：$(*x*, *y* - 1)$、$(*x*, *y* + 1)$、$(*x* - 1, *y*)$ 和 $(*x* + 1, *y*)$，前提是要前往的单元格不是墙。

## 输入格式

第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *m* ≤ 1500$），分别表示小男孩用来周期性铺满平面的迷宫的高度和宽度。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行中，每行包含 $*m*$ 个字符，表示迷宫。每个字符要么是表示墙的 `#`，要么是表示可通行单元格的 `.`，要么是表示小男孩起点的 `S`。

起点所在的单元格可以通行。保证输入中字符 `S` 恰好出现一次。

## 输出格式

如果小男孩能够走到无限远离起点的位置，输出 `Yes`（不含引号）；否则输出 `No`（不含引号）。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，小男孩可以一直向上走，因为存在一条竖直方向的“畅通路径”。他只需无限重复以下步骤：上、上、左、上、上、右、上。

在第二个样例中，竖直方向的路径被阻断了。向左的路径也行不通——下一个迷宫副本会困住小男孩。
